0.content: Donatello, Chevreuse's father, was a Garde praised by everyone as upright. He worked from early morning to late night and came home with sweets and apologies. During a major case he leaked secret intelligence to the press, hoping the public interest would help catch the criminal. His colleagues searched the house, a court convicted him, and he was exiled to the Fortress of Meropide. His wife and daughter fell into poverty in the Fleuve Cendre, where his former colleagues quietly helped them and campaigned so he would not be punished further. After serving his sentence he joined the Special Patrol and trained Chevreuse harshly. She passed every trial, including swims in freezing winter seas, and he decided she was more fit to uphold justice than he was.

1.content: Vice Captain Grizzetti of the Special Patrol had been close to Donatello and looked after Chevreuse, who called him "Uncle Grizzetti". Although she topped her class, he kept her off field missions because her idea of justice was "an eye for an eye". Short-handed one stormy night, he finally took her on a hunt for a notorious gang. A hidden shooter killed him. Chevreuse shot back at the muzzle flash, then stood over the wounded killer, alone in the rain, with her musket aimed between his eyes. She lowered it and arrested him, and shot him in the right leg when he tried to flee. Afterwards she found a Pyro Vision hanging from the stock.

2.comment: Chevreuse: Special Security and Surveillance Patrol
2.content: The Special Security and Surveillance Patrol is a branch of the Maison Gardiennage that apprehends violent criminals the ordinary Gardes cannot handle. It does not do routine street patrols, investigates less than it arrests, and works with the Marechaussee Phantom. Members need not wear uniforms outside formal occasions or carry standard weapons. Under Chevreuse most carry muskets, refuse Gardemek support, and must also pass unarmed-combat standards. The Patrol accepts the descendants of disgraced criminals, and Chevreuse invites even serious felons to act as "special consultants", which the rest of the Maison Gardiennage resents. Her stock reply: "The greatest insult to the law is a criminal roaming free and unpunished."

3.content: After her father's conviction Chevreuse and her mother lived in the Fleuve Cendre, the poor district beneath the Court of Fontaine. She worked for a kind shop owner while a neighbouring couple helped care for her ailing mother. The local children brought her their quarrels as a joke; she came back with legal books and a notebook and heard both sides properly, then personally saw her rulings carried out. She says growing up there showed her how much of Fontaine stays in shadow, and taught her many ways to make justice stick.

4.content: Chiori, the designer who owns Chioriya Boutique, is one of Chevreuse's closest working friends. Chiori's network has given the Patrol intelligence more than once. In return, Chevreuse turns a blind eye when Chiori throws someone out of her shop or drives off a malignant competitor. She notes that Chiori is always in the right and just doesn't bother explaining. Chiori finds working with her a cinch. It was Chiori who brought her into the 4.3 film.

5.comment: Chevreuse: Roses and Muskets and the Rainbow Rose murder
5.content: In the limited-time 4.3 event, Chiori recruited Chevreuse as a musket consultant for Xavier's film of the novel "The Two Musketeers", directed by Furina. When Kamisato Ayato withdrew, she took the lead role of the elder sister Tulipe opposite Ayaka's Iris. At the same time she was privately investigating a murder that copied the novel: a Rainbow Rose left on a victim from the Fleuve Cendre. With the Traveler's help, Emilie's analysis traced the rose to the novelist Baptiste, who confessed falsely.
